subject: POC extension options: phased top‑up vs SKU bundle
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pulseai.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@pulseai.com
Date: 2026-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Short POC extension - proposal request

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're across the initial POC milestones but need a small extension to finish integration checks and run final accuracy tests. Our engineering lead expects ~2-3 weeks of additional run time. Before we escalate to procurement, can you outline options you typically offer for short time‑boxed extensions? Specifically: a) add 3 weeks to the existing timebox at a discounted rate, b) purchase an interim SKU bundle (top‑up) we can consume immediately, or c) convert remaining evaluation credits into a milestone‑based topup (we pay on milestone completion).

Our procurement team will weigh cost predictability vs speed — if you can include clear pros/cons and an updated SOW/price table we can move quickly.

Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of AI Ops — Pulse AI
jordan.lee@pulseai.com
[Attachment: current_poc_summary.pdf (pdf, 320KB)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pulseai.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short POC extension - proposal request

Jordan —

Appreciate the note and congrats to the team on reaching the milestones. We generally support all three approaches you listed; below are pragmatic tradeoffs and an initial numeric example (see attached matrix for line items).

Option A — Timebox extension (3 weeks):
- Pros: keeps single POC agreement intact, minimal procurement paperwork (amendment), predictable monthly invoice.
- Cons: higher per-week rate vs bulk SKU; requires date amendment to SOW.
- Example: 3 weeks @ 15% discount vs list week rate.

Option B — SKU bundle (top‑up):
- Pros: immediate capacity, can be consumed granularly, easier to convert to production SKU later.
- Cons: can be slightly less predictable if usage spikes.
- Example: 500 compute‑hours SKU at 20% off list for Pulse AI.

Option C — Convert credits to milestone top‑up:
- Pros: aligns payment to outcomes, good if procurement needs milestone invoices.
- Cons: requires clear milestone definitions + acceptance criteria; we need signoff on milestone checklist before release.
- Example: convert remaining credits + add $X milestone pool; invoice per milestone completion.

I've attached a pricing_matrix.xlsx with the dollar math and a draft amendment (SOW_draft_v3.pdf) we can send to procurement. If Pulse prefers milestones, please send the expected milestone acceptance criteria (one pager) and procurement contact — we'll build the DocuSign SOW and a lightweight acceptance checklist into the amendment.

Next step: which option feels best for Pulse? If you want, Rafael can propose the exact amendment language and approval path for procurement.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
T: +1 415 555 0186
[Attachment: pricing_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-30T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Short POC extension - proposal request

Looping in recommended commercial language — copying Grace for approval on margins. My suggestion to accelerate procurement: offer two clean paths and let procurement choose.

Path 1 (fastest): Timebox amendment — 3 weeks at list_week_rate * 0.90 (10% discount). No change to milestones or acceptance process. Amendment + PO, 7 business day turnaround.

Path 2 (preferred for procurement): Milestone top‑up — convert existing credits and create 3 discrete milestones (integration smoke, accuracy >= target, production handoff). Price each milestone; offer 25% off the SKU price for the first milestone only (to offset migration friction). Require signoff on checklist per milestone. Prepare SOW_draft_v3.pdf and route via DocuSign.

If they pick Path 2 we should also include a short clause about runout/consumption (unused top‑up credit expires 60 days after final milestone or converts at list rate). Grace — ok to approve the 25% initial milestone concession?

— Rafael

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pulseai.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@pulseai.com
Date: 2026-07-01T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short POC extension - proposal request

Vanessa / Rafael —

Thanks for the clear options. Procurement prefers Path 2 (milestone top‑up) because they can align release of funds to acceptance, which helps our internal approvers. We will: 1) commit to three milestones (integration checks, model accuracy >= 92% on holdout, production checklist complete), 2) accept the 25% concession on the first milestone, and 3) expect a DocuSign SOW and acceptance checklist by end of week. Procurement contact is Maria Chen (maria.chen@pulseai.com).

Please route the SOW_draft_v3.pdf to Maria and cc me. Once Maria confirms, we'll raise a PO.

Jordan
